page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u1-c1m2.4xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.5 GHz, supported by a 33 MB L3 cache. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a 2.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data places this instance in the average performance tier across multiple workloads. In CPU-focused tests, the server achieved a stress-ng single-core score of 1876.98 and a multi-core score of 15440.75, supported by a PassMark CPU score of 19226.97. Memory performance shows a read-only small block cached bandwidth of 831.5 GB/sec, which drops to 84.73 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write bandwidth of 54.87 GB/sec. For specialized tasks, the system handles single-threaded gzip compression at 27.58 GB/sec and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 79.72 GB/sec.

Given its dedicated 16-core Intel Xeon architecture and 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the ecs.u1-c1m2.4xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory profile suitable for compute-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. It demonstrates solid capabilities in database operations, scoring 7793.61 on PassMark database tests, and handles Redis SET operations at 15.82 million operations per second. This makes the instance well-suited for web serving, medium-scale database hosting, and lightweight machine learning inference, where it processed 7B model prompts at 32.03 tokens per second. The lack of bundled local storage means users must provision external block storage, representing a structural tradeoff for storage-heavy applications.
